import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Grothendieck–Katz p-curvature conjecture

*References:*
- [Wikipedia, Grothendieck–Katz p-curvature conjecture](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grothendieck%E2%80%93Katz_p-curvature_conjecture)
- [Chambert-Loir, *Théorèmes d'algébrisation en géométrie diophantienne*](https://arxiv.org/abs/math/0103192)
- [Di Vizio, *Arithmetic theory of q-difference equations*](https://arxiv.org/abs/math/0104178)
-/

namespace GrothendieckKatzPCurvatureConjecture

/-- Formal differentiation of a rational function in its indeterminate. -/
noncomputable def ratFuncDeriv (K : Type*) [Field K] (f : RatFunc K) : RatFunc K :=
  let n := f.num
  let d := f.denom
  (algebraMap (Polynomial K) (RatFunc K) (n.derivative * d - n * d.derivative)) /
    algebraMap (Polynomial K) (RatFunc K) (d ^ 2)

/-- The sequence $A_0=I$, $A_1=A$, and $A_{m+1}=A_m'+A_mA$ associated to
$Y'=AY$. Its $p$th term after reduction modulo $p$ is the $p$-curvature matrix. -/
noncomputable def iteratedSystemMatrix {K : Type*} [Field K] {n : ℕ}
    (A : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) (RatFunc K)) : ℕ → Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) (RatFunc K)
  | 0 => 1
  | 1 => A
  | m + 2 => (iteratedSystemMatrix A (m + 1)).map (ratFuncDeriv K) +
      iteratedSystemMatrix A (m + 1) * A

/-- A rational function over `ZMod p` is a reduction of one over $\mathbb Q$ if both
come from the same quotient of integer polynomials and the denominator remains nonzero
modulo $p$. -/
def IsReductionAt (p : ℕ) (hp : p.Prime) (a : RatFunc ℚ)
    (aₚ : RatFunc (ZMod p)) : Prop :=
  letI : Fact p.Prime := ⟨hp⟩
  ∃ f g : Polynomial ℤ,
    g.map (Int.castRingHom (ZMod p)) ≠ 0 ∧
    a = RatFunc.mk (f.map (Int.castRingHom ℚ)) (g.map (Int.castRingHom ℚ)) ∧
    aₚ = RatFunc.mk (f.map (Int.castRingHom (ZMod p))) (g.map (Int.castRingHom (ZMod p)))

/-- A rational-function matrix has zero $p$-curvature at a prime $p$ if it has a good
reduction modulo $p$ whose $p$th iterated system matrix vanishes. -/
def HasZeroPCurvatureAt {n : ℕ} (A : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) (RatFunc ℚ))
    (p : ℕ) (hp : p.Prime) : Prop :=
  letI : Fact p.Prime := ⟨hp⟩
  ∃ Aₚ : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) (RatFunc (ZMod p)),
    (∀ i j, IsReductionAt p hp (A i j) (Aₚ i j)) ∧ iteratedSystemMatrix Aₚ p = 0

/-- The system $Y'=AY$ has a full set of solutions algebraic over $\mathbb Q(z)$ if
there is an invertible fundamental matrix over an algebraic closure of $\mathbb Q(z)$.
The derivation in the algebraic closure is required to extend formal differentiation. -/
def HasAlgebraicFundamentalMatrix {n : ℕ}
    (A : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) (RatFunc ℚ)) : Prop :=
  let K := AlgebraicClosure (RatFunc ℚ)
  ∃ D : Derivation ℚ K K,
    (∀ f : RatFunc ℚ,
      D (algebraMap (RatFunc ℚ) K f) = algebraMap (RatFunc ℚ) K (ratFuncDeriv ℚ f)) ∧
    ∃ Y : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) K,
      Y.det ≠ 0 ∧ Y.map D = A.map (algebraMap (RatFunc ℚ) K) * Y

/--
**Grothendieck–Katz $p$-curvature conjecture (essential case).** Let $n>0$ and let
$A\in M_n(\mathbb Q(z))$. If, for all but finitely many primes $p$, $A$ has good
reduction modulo $p$ and the reduced system $Y'=A_pY$ has zero $p$-curvature
(equivalently, a fundamental matrix in $\mathbb F_p(z)$), then $Y'=AY$ has a
fundamental matrix whose entries are algebraic over $\mathbb Q(z)$.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 12 13 34]
theorem grothendieck_katz_p_curvature_conjecture {n : ℕ} (hn : 0 < n)
    (A : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) (RatFunc ℚ))
    (hA : ∀ᶠ p : Nat.Primes in Filter.cofinite,
      HasZeroPCurvatureAt A p p.property) :
    HasAlgebraicFundamentalMatrix A := by
  sorry

end GrothendieckKatzPCurvatureConjecture

Restricted to n > 0 because the source speaks of a vector system of positive size; this avoids introducing the vacuous zero-dimensional system.

import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Grothendieck–Katz $p$-curvature conjecture

A local-global principle for linear ordinary differential equations, conjectured by
Grothendieck around 1969 and first published by Katz in 1972.

In its essential case the conjecture concerns a linear differential system
$$\frac{dY}{dz} = A(z)\,Y, \qquad A \in M_n(\mathbb{Q}(z)).$$
Define the matrices $A_k \in M_n(\mathbb{Q}(z))$ by $A_0 = I$ and $A_{k+1} = A_k' + A_k A$, so that
every solution satisfies $Y^{(k)} = A_k Y$. For a prime $p$ not dividing any denominator of $A$,
the matrix $A_p$ modulo $p$ is the *$p$-curvature* of the system reduced modulo $p$, and (Cartier)
it vanishes if and only if the reduced system has a full set of solutions in $\mathbb{F}_p(z)$.
This is a necessary condition, for all but finitely many $p$, for the original system to have a
full set of solutions algebraic over $\mathbb{Q}(z)$. Grothendieck's conjecture is that it is
also sufficient.

Katz reformulated the conjecture in terms of the Lie algebra of the (generic) differential
Galois group of the system, which should be the smallest algebraic Lie subalgebra of
$\mathfrak{gl}_n$ whose reduction modulo $p$ contains the $p$-curvature for almost all $p$.
The general case is open.

*References:*
- [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grothendieck%E2%80%93Katz_p-curvature_conjecture)
- N. M. Katz, *Algebraic solutions of differential equations ($p$-curvature and the Hodge
  filtration)*, Invent. Math. 18 (1972), 1–118.
- N. M. Katz, *A conjecture in the arithmetic theory of differential equations*,
  Bull. Soc. Math. France 110 (1982), 203–239.
- A. Chambert-Loir, *Théorèmes d'algébrisation en géométrie diophantienne*, Séminaire Bourbaki,
  Exp. 886, [arXiv:math/0103192](https://arxiv.org/abs/math/0103192), §3.
- L. Di Vizio, *Arithmetic theory of $q$-difference equations*, Invent. Math. 150 (2002),
  [arXiv:math/0104178](https://arxiv.org/abs/math/0104178), Introduction.

TODO: Katz's reformulation (Katz 1982, Conj. 9.2) in terms of the Lie algebra of the generic
differential Galois group. This needs algebraic groups over $\mathbb{Q}(z)$ and their Lie
algebras, which are not available.
-/

open Polynomial
open scoped Differential

namespace GrothendieckKatzPCurvatureConjecture

-- The derivation `d/dz` on the field of rational functions.

section RatFuncDeriv

variable {K : Type*} [Field K]

/-- The derivative $f' = (P'Q - PQ')/Q^2$ of a rational function $f = P/Q$, computed from its
reduced numerator and denominator. -/
noncomputable def ratFuncDerivFun (f : RatFunc K) : RatFunc K :=
  algebraMap K[X] (RatFunc K) (derivative f.num * f.denom - f.num * derivative f.denom) /
    algebraMap K[X] (RatFunc K) (f.denom ^ 2)

/-- The quotient rule holds for an arbitrary representation $f = P/Q$ with $Q \ne 0$. -/
@[category API, AMS 12]
lemma ratFuncDerivFun_div (p q : K[X]) (hq : q ≠ 0) :
    ratFuncDerivFun (algebraMap K[X] (RatFunc K) p / algebraMap K[X] (RatFunc K) q) =
      algebraMap K[X] (RatFunc K) (derivative p * q - p * derivative q) /
        algebraMap K[X] (RatFunc K) (q ^ 2) := by
  set f := algebraMap K[X] (RatFunc K) p / algebraMap K[X] (RatFunc K) q with hf
  have e : f.num * q = p * f.denom := (RatFunc.num_mul_eq_mul_denom_iff hq).mpr hf
  have e' := congrArg derivative e
  simp only [derivative_mul] at e'
  unfold ratFuncDerivFun
  rw [div_eq_div_iff (RatFunc.algebraMap_ne_zero (pow_ne_zero _ f.denom_ne_zero))
    (RatFunc.algebraMap_ne_zero (pow_ne_zero _ hq)), ← map_mul, ← map_mul]
  congr 1
  linear_combination (q * f.denom) * e' - (derivative f.denom * q + derivative q * f.denom) * e

@[category API, AMS 12]
lemma ratFuncDerivFun_add (a b : RatFunc K) :
    ratFuncDerivFun (a + b) = ratFuncDerivFun a + ratFuncDerivFun b := by
  induction a using RatFunc.induction_on with | f p q hq =>
  induction b using RatFunc.induction_on with | f r s hs =>
  have hq' := RatFunc.algebraMap_ne_zero (K := K) hq
  have hs' := RatFunc.algebraMap_ne_zero (K := K) hs
  rw [div_add_div _ _ hq' hs', ← map_mul, ← map_mul, ← map_add, ← map_mul,
    ratFuncDerivFun_div _ _ (mul_ne_zero hq hs), ratFuncDerivFun_div _ _ hq,
    ratFuncDerivFun_div _ _ hs]
  simp only [derivative_mul, map_sub, map_mul, map_add, map_pow]
  field_simp
  ring

@[category API, AMS 12]
lemma ratFuncDerivFun_mul (a b : RatFunc K) :
    ratFuncDerivFun (a * b) = a * ratFuncDerivFun b + b * ratFuncDerivFun a := by
  induction a using RatFunc.induction_on with | f p q hq =>
  induction b using RatFunc.induction_on with | f r s hs =>
  have hq' := RatFunc.algebraMap_ne_zero (K := K) hq
  have hs' := RatFunc.algebraMap_ne_zero (K := K) hs
  rw [div_mul_div_comm, ← map_mul, ← map_mul,
    ratFuncDerivFun_div _ _ (mul_ne_zero hq hs), ratFuncDerivFun_div _ _ hq,
    ratFuncDerivFun_div _ _ hs]
  simp only [derivative_mul, map_sub, map_mul, map_add, map_pow]
  field_simp
  ring

@[category API, AMS 12]
lemma ratFuncDerivFun_zero : ratFuncDerivFun (0 : RatFunc K) = 0 := by
  have := ratFuncDerivFun_add (0 : RatFunc K) 0
  rw [add_zero] at this
  exact left_eq_add.mp this

/-- The field of rational functions `RatFunc K` is a differential field for the derivation
$d/dz$, written `f′`. -/
noncomputable instance instDifferentialRatFunc : Differential (RatFunc K) where
  deriv := @Derivation.mk' ℤ _ (RatFunc K) _ (Ring.toIntAlgebra _) _ _ _ _
    (AddMonoidHom.toIntLinearMap
      { toFun := ratFuncDerivFun
        map_zero' := ratFuncDerivFun_zero
        map_add' := ratFuncDerivFun_add })
    fun a b => ratFuncDerivFun_mul a b

/-- On polynomials, the derivation `f′` on `RatFunc K` is the usual polynomial derivative. -/
@[category API, AMS 12]
lemma deriv_algebraMap_polynomial (p : K[X]) :
    (algebraMap K[X] (RatFunc K) p : RatFunc K)′ = algebraMap K[X] (RatFunc K) (derivative p) := by
  change ratFuncDerivFun _ = _
  simpa using ratFuncDerivFun_div p 1 one_ne_zero

@[category test, AMS 12]
lemma deriv_X : (RatFunc.X : RatFunc K)′ = 1 := by
  rw [← RatFunc.algebraMap_X, deriv_algebraMap_polynomial]
  simp

end RatFuncDeriv

-- The `p`-curvature of a linear differential system.

variable {n : ℕ}

/-- `iterDerivMatrix A k` is the matrix $A_k \in M_n(\mathbb{Q}(z))$ defined by the recurrence
$A_0 = I$, $A_{k+1} = A_k' + A_k A$. Every solution $Y$ of the system $Y' = AY$ satisfies
$Y^{(k)} = A_k Y$. For a prime $p$, the matrix $A_p$ is the *$p$-curvature matrix* of the
system: when $A$ can be reduced modulo $p$, the reduction of $A_p$ vanishes exactly when the
$p$-curvature $\nabla(d/dz)^p$ of the reduced system vanishes, i.e. exactly when the reduced
system has a full set of solutions in $\mathbb{F}_p(z)$ (Cartier). -/
noncomputable def iterDerivMatrix (A : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) (RatFunc ℚ)) :
    ℕ → Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) (RatFunc ℚ)
  | 0 => 1
  | k + 1 => (iterDerivMatrix A k).map (fun f ↦ f′) + iterDerivMatrix A k * A

@[category test, AMS 12 34]
lemma iterDerivMatrix_zero (A : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) (RatFunc ℚ)) : iterDerivMatrix A 0 = 1 :=
  rfl

@[category test, AMS 12 34]
lemma iterDerivMatrix_one (A : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) (RatFunc ℚ)) : iterDerivMatrix A 1 = A := by
  ext i j
  simp only [iterDerivMatrix, Matrix.add_apply, Matrix.map_apply, Matrix.one_apply, Matrix.one_mul]
  split_ifs <;> simp

/-- A rational function $f \in \mathbb{Q}(z)$ is *zero modulo `p`* if $f = P/Q$ with
$P, Q \in \mathbb{Z}[z]$, $Q \not\equiv 0 \pmod p$ and $P \equiv 0 \pmod p$. For a prime $p$ this
says that $f$ can be reduced modulo $p$ and its reduction in $\mathbb{F}_p(z)$ is zero;
equivalently, the $p$-adic Gauss norm of $f$ is $< 1$. -/
def IsZeroModP (p : ℕ) (f : RatFunc ℚ) : Prop :=
  ∃ P Q : ℤ[X], Q.map (Int.castRingHom (ZMod p)) ≠ 0 ∧ P.map (Int.castRingHom (ZMod p)) = 0 ∧
    f = algebraMap ℚ[X] (RatFunc ℚ) (P.map (Int.castRingHom ℚ)) /
      algebraMap ℚ[X] (RatFunc ℚ) (Q.map (Int.castRingHom ℚ))

@[category test, AMS 12]
lemma isZeroModP_zero (p : ℕ) [Fact p.Prime] : IsZeroModP p 0 :=
  ⟨0, 1, by simp, by simp, by simp⟩

@[category test, AMS 12]
lemma isZeroModP_natCast (p : ℕ) [Fact p.Prime] : IsZeroModP p (p : RatFunc ℚ) :=
  ⟨p, 1, by simp, by simp, by simp⟩

@[category test, AMS 12]
lemma not_isZeroModP_one (p : ℕ) [Fact p.Prime] : ¬ IsZeroModP p 1 := by
  rintro ⟨P, Q, hQ, hP, h⟩
  have hinj := Polynomial.map_injective _ (Int.castRingHom ℚ).injective_int
  have hQ' : Q.map (Int.castRingHom ℚ) ≠ 0 := by
    intro h0
    have : Q = 0 := hinj (by simpa using h0)
    simp [this] at hQ
  rw [eq_div_iff (RatFunc.algebraMap_ne_zero hQ'), one_mul] at h
  rw [hinj (RatFunc.algebraMap_injective ℚ h)] at hQ
  exact hQ hP

/-- The system $Y' = AY$, $A \in M_n(\mathbb{Q}(z))$, has *$p$-curvature zero for almost all
$p$*: for all but finitely many primes $p$, every entry of the $p$-curvature matrix $A_p$ is zero
modulo $p$. Since $A$ itself can be reduced modulo $p$ for all but finitely many $p$, this is
equivalent (Cartier) to asking that, for all but finitely many primes $p$, the system reduced
modulo $p$ has a full set of solutions in $\mathbb{F}_p(z)$. -/
def HasPCurvatureZeroForAlmostAllPrimes (A : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) (RatFunc ℚ)) : Prop :=
  ∀ᶠ p in Filter.cofinite, p.Prime → ∀ i j, IsZeroModP p (iterDerivMatrix A p i j)

/-- The system $Y' = AY$, $A \in M_n(\mathbb{Q}(z))$, has a *full set of solutions algebraic over
$\mathbb{Q}(z)$*: there is an algebraic extension field $L$ of $\mathbb{Q}(z)$, equipped with the
(unique) extension of $d/dz$ to a derivation of $L$, and a fundamental matrix
$Y \in GL_n(L)$ with $Y' = AY$. Equivalently, the differential module $(\mathbb{Q}(z)^n, d/dz - A)$
becomes trivial over an algebraic extension of $\mathbb{Q}(z)$. -/
def HasFullSetOfAlgebraicSolutions (A : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) (RatFunc ℚ)) : Prop :=
  ∃ (L : Type) (_ : Field L) (_ : Algebra (RatFunc ℚ) L) (_ : Differential L),
    DifferentialAlgebra (RatFunc ℚ) L ∧ Algebra.IsAlgebraic (RatFunc ℚ) L ∧
    ∃ Y : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) L,
      IsUnit Y ∧ Y.map (fun y ↦ y′) = A.map (algebraMap (RatFunc ℚ) L) * Y

/-- **Grothendieck–Katz $p$-curvature conjecture** (Grothendieck, 1969; Katz, 1972).

Let $A \in M_n(\mathbb{Q}(z))$ and consider the linear differential system $Y' = A(z)Y$.
Let $A_0 = I$ and $A_{k+1} = A_k' + A_k A$, so that $A_p$ is the $p$-curvature matrix of the
system. If for all but finitely many primes $p$ the $p$-curvature $A_p$ vanishes modulo $p$
(equivalently, the system reduced modulo $p$ has a full set of solutions in $\mathbb{F}_p(z)$),
then the system has a full set of solutions algebraic over $\mathbb{Q}(z)$, i.e. a fundamental
matrix $Y \in GL_n(L)$ with $Y' = AY$ for some algebraic extension $L$ of $\mathbb{Q}(z)$.

The converse is classical; see `grothendieck_katz_p_curvature_conjecture.variants.necessity`. -/
@[category research open, AMS 12 14 34]
theorem grothendieck_katz_p_curvature_conjecture (A : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) (RatFunc ℚ))
    (hA : HasPCurvatureZeroForAlmostAllPrimes A) : HasFullSetOfAlgebraicSolutions A := by
  sorry

/-- The classical necessity direction (Cartier, Katz): if the system $Y' = AY$ with
$A \in M_n(\mathbb{Q}(z))$ has a full set of solutions algebraic over $\mathbb{Q}(z)$, then for
all but finitely many primes $p$ its $p$-curvature $A_p$ vanishes modulo $p$. -/
@[category research solved, AMS 12 14 34]
theorem grothendieck_katz_p_curvature_conjecture.variants.necessity
    (A : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) (RatFunc ℚ)) (hA : HasFullSetOfAlgebraicSolutions A) :
    HasPCurvatureZeroForAlmostAllPrimes A := by
  sorry

end GrothendieckKatzPCurvatureConjecture
attempts.decomposition_objections: No substantive objection. Two remarks: (1) the notes for the primary slot phrase the hypothesis as 'all p for which A can be reduced and A_p ≡ 0 mod p / the reduced system has a full set of solutions in 𝔽_p(z)'; pointwise these are not identical to 'A_p ≡ 0 mod p' (A_p can vanish mod p for a non-p-integral A), but under the cofinite quantifier all three readings coincide, and the Lean file uses the p-curvature reading. (2) The Katz Galois-group slot is correctly identified as an equivalent reformulation, but it cannot be stated faithfully with current primitives (no algebraic groups/Lie algebras/Tannakian Galois group in Mathlib), so it is omitted rather than approximated.
modeling_decisions: Formalized the 'essential case' A ∈ M_n(ℚ(z)) (rational functions, rational coefficients) as the decomposition table prescribes; the article says the algebraic-function/number-field version reduces to it.
'Almost all p' = all but finitely many primes: `∀ᶠ p in Filter.cofinite, p.Prime → …` on ℕ (not merely infinitely many).

The mod-p condition is 'A_p ≡ 0 mod p' in the Gauss-norm sense (IsZeroModP on each entry), following Wikipedia's 'p-curvature of 0 for almost all p' and Chambert-Loir's equivalence with the reduced system having a basis of solutions in 𝔽_p(z). I did NOT add the pointwise requirement 'A can be reduced mod p': it holds automatically for all but finitely many p, so the cofinite hypothesis is unchanged (note: pointwise it is not implied — e.g. A = [[0,1/p],[0,0]] has A_k = 0 for k ≥ 2 — which is why the definition docstrings only claim the cofinite equivalence).

'Full set of algebraic solutions' = invertible matrix solution Y ∈ GL_n(L) (`IsUnit Y`) over some algebraic extension field L of ℚ(z) equipped with a derivation extending d/dz. The derivation on an algebraic extension in characteristic 0 exists and is unique, so the extra existential over `Differential L` with `DifferentialAlgebra (RatFunc ℚ) L` adds no freedom. Allowing arbitrary algebraic (not nec. finite) L is equivalent, since the finitely many entries of Y generate a finite subextension closed under the derivation. Over a field, IsUnit Y ⟺ det Y ≠ 0 ⟺ columns independent over constants (Wronskian).

import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Grothendieck–Katz $p$-curvature conjecture

A conjectured local–global principle for linear ordinary differential equations.

Consider a linear differential system
$$\frac{dY}{dz} = A(z)\,Y, \qquad A \in M_n(\mathbb{Q}(z)).$$
For almost all primes $p$ the matrix $A$ can be reduced modulo $p$, giving a system over
$\mathbb{F}_p(z)$. The *$p$-curvature* of the reduced system is the matrix $A_p \bmod p$, where
$A_0 = 1$ and $A_{k+1} = A_k' + A_k A$ (so that $Y^{(k)} = A_k Y$ for every solution $Y$).
By a theorem of Cartier and Katz, the reduced system has a full set of solutions in
$\mathbb{F}_p(z)$ if and only if its $p$-curvature vanishes.

If the original system has a full set of solutions algebraic over $\mathbb{Q}(z)$, then its
$p$-curvature vanishes for almost all $p$. Grothendieck's conjecture is the converse:
if the $p$-curvature vanishes for almost all primes $p$, then the system has a full set of
algebraic solutions, i.e. a fundamental matrix with entries algebraic over $\mathbb{Q}(z)$.

The general case (a system with coefficients algebraic functions over a number field, or an
integrable connection on a smooth variety over a number field) reduces to this one.

*References:*
* [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grothendieck%E2%80%93Katz_p-curvature_conjecture)
* N. M. Katz, *Algebraic solutions of differential equations ($p$-curvature and the Hodge
  filtration)*, Invent. Math. 18 (1972), 1–118.
* N. M. Katz, *A conjecture in the arithmetic theory of differential equations*,
  Bull. Soc. Math. France 110 (1982), 203–239.
* A. Chambert-Loir, *Théorèmes d'algébrisation en géométrie diophantienne*,
  Séminaire Bourbaki, Exp. 886, [arXiv:math/0103192](https://arxiv.org/abs/math/0103192).
* L. Di Vizio, *Arithmetic theory of $q$-difference equations*, Invent. Math. 150 (2002),
  [arXiv:math/0104178](https://arxiv.org/abs/math/0104178).
-/

open scoped Polynomial Differential

namespace GrothendieckKatzPCurvatureConjecture

section Derivative

variable {K : Type*} [Field K]

/-- The derivative $\frac{d}{dz}$ of a rational function $f = g / h \in K(z)$, given by the
quotient rule $(g' h - g h') / h^2$ applied to the reduced numerator and denominator of $f$. -/
noncomputable def derivative (f : RatFunc K) : RatFunc K :=
  algebraMap K[X] (RatFunc K)
      (Polynomial.derivative f.num * f.denom - f.num * Polynomial.derivative f.denom) /
    algebraMap K[X] (RatFunc K) (f.denom ^ 2)

/-- The quotient rule holds for any representation $f = p / q$, not only the reduced one. -/
@[category API, AMS 12]
theorem derivative_div (p : K[X]) {q : K[X]} (hq : q ≠ 0) :
    derivative (algebraMap K[X] (RatFunc K) p / algebraMap K[X] (RatFunc K) q) =
      algebraMap K[X] (RatFunc K) (Polynomial.derivative p * q - p * Polynomial.derivative q) /
        algebraMap K[X] (RatFunc K) (q ^ 2) := by
  set x := algebraMap K[X] (RatFunc K) p / algebraMap K[X] (RatFunc K) q with hx
  have h1 : x.num * q = p * x.denom := (RatFunc.num_mul_eq_mul_denom_iff hq).mpr hx
  have h2 := congrArg Polynomial.derivative h1
  simp only [Polynomial.derivative_mul] at h2
  unfold derivative
  rw [div_eq_div_iff (RatFunc.algebraMap_ne_zero (pow_ne_zero 2 x.denom_ne_zero))
    (RatFunc.algebraMap_ne_zero (pow_ne_zero 2 hq)), ← map_mul, ← map_mul]
  congr 1
  linear_combination (x.denom * q) * h2 -
    (Polynomial.derivative x.denom * q + x.denom * Polynomial.derivative q) * h1

@[category API, AMS 12]
theorem derivative_algebraMap (g : K[X]) :
    derivative (algebraMap K[X] (RatFunc K) g) =
      algebraMap K[X] (RatFunc K) (Polynomial.derivative g) := by
  simp [derivative]

@[category test, AMS 12]
theorem derivative_zero : derivative (0 : RatFunc K) = 0 := by
  simp [derivative]

@[category test, AMS 12]
theorem derivative_one : derivative (1 : RatFunc K) = 0 := by
  simp [derivative]

@[category test, AMS 12]
theorem derivative_X : derivative (RatFunc.X : RatFunc K) = 1 := by
  rw [← RatFunc.algebraMap_X, derivative_algebraMap]
  simp

@[category test, AMS 12]
theorem derivative_inv_X : derivative ((RatFunc.X : RatFunc K)⁻¹) = -(RatFunc.X ^ 2)⁻¹ := by
  have h : (RatFunc.X : RatFunc K)⁻¹ =
      algebraMap K[X] (RatFunc K) 1 / algebraMap K[X] (RatFunc K) Polynomial.X := by
    simp [RatFunc.algebraMap_X]
  rw [h, derivative_div _ Polynomial.X_ne_zero]
  simp [RatFunc.algebraMap_X]
  rw [neg_div, one_div]

variable {n : ℕ}

/-- For a linear differential system $Y' = A Y$ with $A \in M_n(K(z))$, the matrices $A_k$
defined by $A_0 = 1$ and $A_{k+1} = A_k' + A_k A$. They satisfy $Y^{(k)} = A_k Y$ for every
solution $Y$. -/
noncomputable def derivativeMatrix (A : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) (RatFunc K)) :
    ℕ → Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) (RatFunc K)
  | 0 => 1
  | k + 1 => (derivativeMatrix A k).map derivative + derivativeMatrix A k * A

@[category test, AMS 12]
theorem derivativeMatrix_one (A : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) (RatFunc K)) :
    derivativeMatrix A 1 = A := by
  ext i j
  simp [derivativeMatrix, Matrix.one_apply, apply_ite derivative, derivative_zero, derivative_one]

end Derivative

section Reduction

/-- A rational function $f \in \mathbb{Q}(z)$ is *$p$-integral* if $f = g / h$ with
$g, h \in \mathbb{Z}[z]$ and $h \not\equiv 0 \pmod p$. Such an $f$ can be reduced modulo $p$
to $\bar g / \bar h \in \mathbb{F}_p(z)$. -/
def IsPIntegral (p : ℕ) (f : RatFunc ℚ) : Prop :=
  ∃ g h : ℤ[X], h.map (Int.castRingHom (ZMod p)) ≠ 0 ∧
    f = Polynomial.aeval (RatFunc.X : RatFunc ℚ) g / Polynomial.aeval (RatFunc.X : RatFunc ℚ) h

/-- A rational function $f \in \mathbb{Q}(z)$ is *zero modulo $p$* if $f = p \cdot g$ with $g$
$p$-integral. Equivalently, $f$ is $p$-integral and its reduction in $\mathbb{F}_p(z)$ is $0$. -/
def IsZeroMod (p : ℕ) (f : RatFunc ℚ) : Prop :=
  ∃ g : RatFunc ℚ, IsPIntegral p g ∧ f = p * g

@[category API, AMS 12]
theorem aeval_X_injective :
    Function.Injective (Polynomial.aeval (RatFunc.X : RatFunc ℚ) : ℤ[X] → RatFunc ℚ) := by
  intro a b hab
  have key : ∀ q : ℤ[X], Polynomial.aeval (RatFunc.X : RatFunc ℚ) q =
      algebraMap ℚ[X] (RatFunc ℚ) (q.map (Int.castRingHom ℚ)) := fun q ↦ by
    rw [← RatFunc.algebraMap_X, Polynomial.aeval_algebraMap_apply,
      Polynomial.aeval_X_left_eq_map, algebraMap_int_eq]
  rw [key, key] at hab
  exact Polynomial.map_injective _ Int.cast_injective
    (IsFractionRing.injective ℚ[X] (RatFunc ℚ) hab)

@[category test, AMS 11 12]
theorem isPIntegral_aeval (p : ℕ) [Fact p.Prime] (g : ℤ[X]) :
    IsPIntegral p (Polynomial.aeval (RatFunc.X : RatFunc ℚ) g) :=
  ⟨g, 1, by simp, by simp⟩

@[category test, AMS 11 12]
theorem isZeroMod_natCast (p : ℕ) [Fact p.Prime] : IsZeroMod p (p : RatFunc ℚ) :=
  ⟨1, ⟨1, 1, by simp, by simp⟩, by simp⟩

@[category test, AMS 11 12]
theorem not_isPIntegral_half : ¬ IsPIntegral 2 (1 / 2 : RatFunc ℚ) := by
  rintro ⟨g, h, hh, hf⟩
  have hh0 : Polynomial.aeval (RatFunc.X : RatFunc ℚ) h ≠ 0 := by
    rintro h0
    rw [← map_zero (Polynomial.aeval (RatFunc.X : RatFunc ℚ) : ℤ[X] →ₐ[ℤ] RatFunc ℚ),
      aeval_X_injective.eq_iff] at h0
    simp [h0] at hh
  have : h = 2 * g := by
    apply aeval_X_injective
    field_simp at hf
    rw [map_mul, map_ofNat]
    linear_combination hf
  subst this
  have : (2 : (ZMod 2)[X]) = 0 := by
    have : (2 : ZMod 2) = 0 := by decide
    rw [← Polynomial.C_ofNat, this, map_zero]
  simp [this] at hh

variable {n : ℕ}

/-- The linear differential system $Y' = A Y$, $A \in M_n(\mathbb{Q}(z))$, *has $p$-curvature
zero*: $A$ can be reduced modulo $p$, and the $p$-curvature $A_p \bmod p$ of the reduced system
vanishes, i.e. $A_p \equiv 0 \pmod p$ entrywise. By a theorem of Cartier and Katz, this holds if
and only if the reduced system $Y' = \bar A Y$ has a full set of solutions in $\mathbb{F}_p(z)$. -/
def HasPCurvatureZero (p : ℕ) (A : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) (RatFunc ℚ)) : Prop :=
  (∀ i j, IsPIntegral p (A i j)) ∧ ∀ i j, IsZeroMod p (derivativeMatrix A p i j)

end Reduction

section Solutions

variable {n : ℕ}

/-- The linear differential system $Y' = A Y$, $A \in M_n(\mathbb{Q}(z))$, *has a full set of
algebraic solutions*: there is a differential field $L$, algebraic over $\mathbb{Q}(z)$ and whose
derivation extends $\frac{d}{dz}$, containing a fundamental matrix of solutions, i.e. an
invertible $Y \in M_n(L)$ with $Y' = A Y$. -/
def HasFullSetOfAlgebraicSolutions (A : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) (RatFunc ℚ)) : Prop :=
  ∃ (L : Type) (_ : Field L) (_ : Algebra (RatFunc ℚ) L) (_ : Differential L),
    Algebra.IsAlgebraic (RatFunc ℚ) L ∧
    (∀ f : RatFunc ℚ,
      (algebraMap (RatFunc ℚ) L f)′ = algebraMap (RatFunc ℚ) L (derivative f)) ∧
    ∃ Y : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) L,
      IsUnit Y ∧ Y.map (fun y ↦ y′) = A.map (algebraMap (RatFunc ℚ) L) * Y

end Solutions

/-- **Grothendieck–Katz $p$-curvature conjecture.** A local–global principle for linear ordinary
differential equations.

Let $A \in M_n(\mathbb{Q}(z))$. If for almost all primes $p$ (all but finitely many) the
reduction modulo $p$ of the linear differential system $Y' = A Y$ has $p$-curvature zero
(equivalently, a full set of solutions in $\mathbb{F}_p(z)$), then the system has a full set of
solutions algebraic over $\mathbb{Q}(z)$, i.e. a fundamental matrix of solutions with entries
in an algebraic extension of $\mathbb{Q}(z)$.

Only this direction is conjectural; the converse is a classical theorem of Katz. -/
@[category research open, AMS 12 14 34]
theorem grothendieck_katz_p_curvature_conjecture {n : ℕ}
    (A : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) (RatFunc ℚ))
    (hA : ∀ᶠ p : Nat.Primes in Filter.cofinite, HasPCurvatureZero p A) :
    HasFullSetOfAlgebraicSolutions A := by
  sorry

end GrothendieckKatzPCurvatureConjecture
attempts.decomposition_objections: None of substance. One remark: the Wikipedia article only describes Katz's Lie-algebra reformulation vaguely ('for a certain wide class of differential equations'); the precise statement for the second slot must come from Katz (1982, Conj. 9.2) as quoted in Di Vizio and Chambert-Loir. I agree with the table that it is an equivalent reformulation subordinate to the primary slot, but it is not statable with existing primitives (no algebraic groups, Lie algebras of algebraic groups, Tannakian Galois groups, or reduction mod p of Lie subalgebras in Mathlib), so it is reported as missing_primitives rather than formalized.
modeling_decisions: The list-page entry is terse; the precise formulation was taken from the article's 'essential case' (Formulation section) and Chambert-Loir §4.1: a system dY/dz = A(z)Y with A ∈ M_n(ℚ(z)), hypothesis 'p-curvature zero for almost all p', conclusion 'full set of algebraic solutions'. The general number-field / connection-on-a-variety form is not stated separately since the article says it reduces to this case.
'Almost all p' is formalized as cofinitely many primes: `∀ᶠ p : Nat.Primes in Filter.cofinite, ...` (not merely infinitely many).

The mod-p condition is stated via p-curvature (A_p ≡ 0 mod p) rather than 'full set of solutions in 𝔽_p(z)'; the article itself says these are the same (Cartier/Katz theorem, Chambert-Loir §4.1 lists the equivalences). A_p is computed over ℚ(z) by the recurrence A_0 = 1, A_{k+1} = A_k' + A_k·A and then reduced; this equals the p-curvature of the reduced system because reduction mod p is a differential ring homomorphism on p-integral rational functions. `HasPCurvatureZero p A` also requires every entry of A to be p-integral (so that 'the reduction mod p of the system' is meaningful); this only excludes finitely many p and so does not change the cofinite hypothesis.

Reduction mod p is encoded without constructing the reduction map: `IsPIntegral p f` means f = g/h with g,h ∈ ℤ[z] and h ≢ 0 mod p (i.e. h.map (Int.castRingHom (ZMod p)) ≠ 0); `IsZeroMod p f` means f = p·g with g p-integral, which is equivalent to 'f is p-integral and its image in 𝔽_p(z) is 0'. For p prime, ZMod p = 𝔽_p; the definitions are only used at primes (for p = 1, IsPIntegral is vacuously false, which never occurs).

'Full set of algebraic solutions' (a fundamental matrix of algebraic functions) is formalized differential-algebraically: ∃ a field L with `Algebra (RatFunc ℚ) L`, `Algebra.IsAlgebraic (RatFunc ℚ) L`, a Mathlib `Differential L` structure whose derivation agrees with d/dz on the image of ℚ(z) (stated for every f ∈ ℚ(z)), and an invertible Y ∈ M_n(L) with entrywise Y′ = A·Y. This is equivalent to the analytic formulation (local holomorphic solutions at a non-singular rational point are algebraic over ℚ(z)) because any finitely generated algebraic differential extension of ℚ(z) embeds, compatibly with d/dz (uniqueness of derivation extension in characteristic 0), into germs of meromorphic functions, and conversely.
The existential is over `L : Type` (universe 0); this loses no generality since any algebraic extension of ℚ(z) is countable and the field generated by the entries of Y is finitely generated.
The derivation on L is Mathlib's `Differential L` (a ℤ-derivation); ℚ-linearity is automatic, so no separate ℚ-linearity hypothesis is imposed.

The bespoke `derivative` on `RatFunc K` is defined via the quotient rule on the reduced numerator/denominator (`RatFunc.num`, `RatFunc.denom`) so that no well-definedness proof is required; `derivative_div` proves the quotient rule for an arbitrary representation p/q, certifying that it is d/dz. It is not packaged as a `Derivation`/`Differential (RatFunc K)` instance (which would have required additivity/Leibniz proofs); the compatibility with L is therefore stated pointwise instead of via `DifferentialAlgebra`.

Katz's reformulation (Katz 1982, Conj. 9.2) says Lie(Gal(M)) is the smallest *algebraic* Lie subalgebra of End_{ℚ(x)}(M) whose reduction mod p contains the p-curvature ψ_p for almost all p. Stating this faithfully needs: (i) the generic (Tannakian) differential Galois group of a connection as an algebraic group over the non-algebraically-closed field ℚ(x) (algebraic subgroup of GL(M) stabilising all horizontal subquotients of all mixed tensor constructions) — Mathlib has no algebraic groups/group schemes, Zariski-closed subgroups of GL_n over a field, or Tannakian machinery; (ii) the Lie algebra of an algebraic group and the notion of an 'algebraic Lie subalgebra' of gl(M) (Lie algebra of some algebraic subgroup), and the fact that a smallest such algebra exists; (iii) reduction modulo p of a Lie subalgebra of End_{ℚ(x)}(M) (spreading out over a finite-type ℤ-algebra lattice) to compare with ψ_p. None of these exist in Mathlib or FormalConjecturesForMathlib; inventing them bespoke would amount to building algebraic-group theory from scratch with a high risk of an unfaithful statement, so the slot is omitted.

import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Grothendieck–Katz $p$-curvature conjecture

A conjectured local–global principle for linear ordinary differential equations: a linear
differential system $dY/dz = A(z)\,Y$ with $A \in M_n(\mathbb{Q}(z))$ has a full set of algebraic
solutions as soon as, for all but finitely many primes $p$, its reduction modulo $p$ has
$p$-curvature zero (equivalently, has a full set of solutions in $\mathbb{F}_p(z)$).

The $p$-curvature is computed by the recurrence $A_0 = I$, $A_{k+1} = A_k' + A_k A$ (so that
$d^kY/dz^k = A_k Y$ for every solution $Y$): the $p$-curvature of the reduction modulo $p$ vanishes
if and only if $A_p \equiv 0 \pmod p$.

*References:*
- [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grothendieck%E2%80%93Katz_p-curvature_conjecture)
- [Wikipedia, List of unsolved problems in mathematics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_unsolved_problems_in_mathematics)
- A. Chambert-Loir, *Théorèmes d'algébrisation en géométrie diophantienne*, Séminaire Bourbaki
  Exp. 886, §6, [arXiv:math/0103192](https://arxiv.org/abs/math/0103192)
- N. M. Katz, *Algebraic solutions of differential equations ($p$-curvature and the Hodge
  filtration)*, Invent. Math. 18 (1972), 1–118
- N. M. Katz, *A conjecture in the arithmetic theory of differential equations*, Bull. Soc. Math.
  France 110 (1982), 203–239
- L. Di Vizio, *Arithmetic theory of $q$-difference equations*, Invent. Math. 150 (2002),
  [arXiv:math/0104178](https://arxiv.org/abs/math/0104178)
-/

namespace GrothendieckKatzPCurvatureConjecture

open Polynomial RatFunc
open scoped Differential

/- ### The differential field `K(X)`

Mathlib has no derivation on `RatFunc K`. We define `d/dX` by the quotient rule on the reduced
numerator and denominator and record it as a `Differential` instance, so that the unique extension
of `d/dX` to finite extensions of `K(X)` (`Differential.differentialFiniteDimensional`) is
available. -/

section RatFuncDerivative

variable {K : Type*} [Field K]

/-- The derivative `d/dX` of a rational function `r = f / g` (with `f = r.num`, `g = r.denom`),
given by the quotient rule `(f' g - f g') / g ^ 2`. -/
noncomputable def ratFuncDerivative (r : RatFunc K) : RatFunc K :=
  (algebraMap K[X] (RatFunc K) (derivative r.num) * algebraMap K[X] (RatFunc K) r.denom -
      algebraMap K[X] (RatFunc K) r.num * algebraMap K[X] (RatFunc K) (derivative r.denom)) /
    algebraMap K[X] (RatFunc K) r.denom ^ 2

/-- The quotient rule holds for any representation `p / q` of a rational function, not only for
the reduced one. -/
@[category API, AMS 12]
theorem ratFuncDerivative_div (p q : K[X]) (hq : q ≠ 0) :
    ratFuncDerivative (algebraMap K[X] (RatFunc K) p / algebraMap K[X] (RatFunc K) q) =
      (algebraMap K[X] (RatFunc K) (derivative p) * algebraMap K[X] (RatFunc K) q -
          algebraMap K[X] (RatFunc K) p * algebraMap K[X] (RatFunc K) (derivative q)) /
        algebraMap K[X] (RatFunc K) q ^ 2 := by
  set r := algebraMap K[X] (RatFunc K) p / algebraMap K[X] (RatFunc K) q with hr
  have h1 : r.num * q = p * r.denom := (num_mul_eq_mul_denom_iff hq).mpr hr
  have h2 : derivative r.num * q + r.num * derivative q =
      derivative p * r.denom + p * derivative r.denom := by
    simpa only [derivative_mul] using congrArg derivative h1
  have key : (derivative r.num * r.denom - r.num * derivative r.denom) * q ^ 2 =
      (derivative p * q - p * derivative q) * r.denom ^ 2 := by
    linear_combination (r.denom * q) * h2 - (derivative q * r.denom + derivative r.denom * q) * h1
  unfold ratFuncDerivative
  rw [div_eq_div_iff (pow_ne_zero 2 (algebraMap_ne_zero (denom_ne_zero r)))
    (pow_ne_zero 2 (algebraMap_ne_zero hq))]
  simpa only [map_mul, map_sub, map_pow] using congrArg (algebraMap K[X] (RatFunc K)) key

@[category API, AMS 12]
theorem ratFuncDerivative_add (x y : RatFunc K) :
    ratFuncDerivative (x + y) = ratFuncDerivative x + ratFuncDerivative y := by
  induction x using RatFunc.induction_on with | _ p₁ q₁ hq₁ => ?_
  induction y using RatFunc.induction_on with | _ p₂ q₂ hq₂ => ?_
  rw [div_add_div _ _ (algebraMap_ne_zero hq₁) (algebraMap_ne_zero hq₂), ← map_mul, ← map_mul,
    ← map_add, ← map_mul, ratFuncDerivative_div _ _ (mul_ne_zero hq₁ hq₂),
    ratFuncDerivative_div _ _ hq₁, ratFuncDerivative_div _ _ hq₂]
  have h₁ := algebraMap_ne_zero (K := K) hq₁
  have h₂ := algebraMap_ne_zero (K := K) hq₂
  simp only [derivative_mul, map_add, map_mul]
  field_simp
  ring

@[category API, AMS 12]
theorem ratFuncDerivative_mul (x y : RatFunc K) :
    ratFuncDerivative (x * y) = x * ratFuncDerivative y + y * ratFuncDerivative x := by
  induction x using RatFunc.induction_on with | _ p₁ q₁ hq₁ => ?_
  induction y using RatFunc.induction_on with | _ p₂ q₂ hq₂ => ?_
  rw [div_mul_div_comm, ← map_mul, ← map_mul, ratFuncDerivative_div _ _ (mul_ne_zero hq₁ hq₂),
    ratFuncDerivative_div _ _ hq₁, ratFuncDerivative_div _ _ hq₂]
  have h₁ := algebraMap_ne_zero (K := K) hq₁
  have h₂ := algebraMap_ne_zero (K := K) hq₂
  simp only [derivative_mul, map_add, map_mul]
  field_simp
  ring

/-- `ratFuncDerivative` as an additive map. -/
noncomputable def ratFuncDerivativeAddHom : RatFunc K →+ RatFunc K :=
  AddMonoidHom.mk' ratFuncDerivative ratFuncDerivative_add

/-- The field `K(X)` of rational functions is a differential field for the derivation `d/dX`. -/
noncomputable instance : Differential (RatFunc K) where
  deriv := @Derivation.mk' ℤ _ (RatFunc K) _ (Ring.toIntAlgebra _) (RatFunc K) _ _ _
    (ratFuncDerivativeAddHom (K := K)).toIntLinearMap ratFuncDerivative_mul

/-- On polynomials, the derivation of `K(X)` is the usual polynomial derivative. -/
@[category API, AMS 12]
theorem deriv_algebraMap_polynomial (f : K[X]) :
    (algebraMap K[X] (RatFunc K) f)′ = algebraMap K[X] (RatFunc K) (derivative f) := by
  change ratFuncDerivative _ = _
  simpa using ratFuncDerivative_div f 1 one_ne_zero

@[category test, AMS 12]
theorem deriv_X : (X : RatFunc K)′ = 1 := by
  rw [← algebraMap_X, deriv_algebraMap_polynomial, derivative_X, map_one]

@[category test, AMS 12]
theorem deriv_C (a : K) : (algebraMap K[X] (RatFunc K) (C a))′ = 0 := by
  rw [deriv_algebraMap_polynomial, derivative_C, map_zero]

end RatFuncDerivative

/- ### The matrices `A_k` and the `p`-curvature -/

section HigherDerivMatrix

variable {R : Type*} [CommRing R] [Differential R] {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]

/-- For a matrix `A` over a differential ring, `higherDerivMatrix A k` is the matrix `A_k` defined
by the recurrence `A_0 = 1`, `A_{k+1} = A_k' + A_k A` (where `A_k'` is the entrywise derivative),
so that every solution `Y` of `Y' = A Y` satisfies `Y^{(k)} = A_k Y`.

For `A` over `ℚ(z)` and a prime `p`, the reduction modulo `p` of `A_p` is the `p`-curvature of
the reduction modulo `p` of the system `Y' = A Y`. -/
noncomputable def higherDerivMatrix (A : Matrix ι ι R) : ℕ → Matrix ι ι R
  | 0 => 1
  | k + 1 => (higherDerivMatrix A k).map (·′) + higherDerivMatrix A k * A

@[category API, AMS 12]
theorem higherDerivMatrix_zero (A : Matrix ι ι R) : higherDerivMatrix A 0 = 1 := rfl

@[category API, AMS 12]
theorem higherDerivMatrix_succ (A : Matrix ι ι R) (k : ℕ) :
    higherDerivMatrix A (k + 1) =
      (higherDerivMatrix A k).map (·′) + higherDerivMatrix A k * A := rfl

@[category test, AMS 12]
theorem higherDerivMatrix_one (A : Matrix ι ι R) : higherDerivMatrix A 1 = A := by
  have : (1 : Matrix ι ι R).map (·′) = 0 := by
    ext i j
    by_cases h : i = j <;> simp [h]
  simp [higherDerivMatrix, this]

end HigherDerivMatrix

/- ### Reduction modulo `p` of rational functions over `ℚ` -/

section ReductionModP

/-- A rational function `r ∈ ℚ(z)` is *`p`-integral* (its reduction modulo `p` is defined) if
`r = f / g` with `f, g ∈ ℤ[z]` and `g ≢ 0 (mod p)`. Equivalently, `r` has `p`-adic Gauss norm
at most `1`. -/
def IsPIntegral (p : ℕ) (r : RatFunc ℚ) : Prop :=
  ∃ f g : ℤ[X], g.map (Int.castRingHom (ZMod p)) ≠ 0 ∧
    r = algebraMap ℚ[X] (RatFunc ℚ) (f.map (Int.castRingHom ℚ)) /
      algebraMap ℚ[X] (RatFunc ℚ) (g.map (Int.castRingHom ℚ))

/-- A rational function `r ∈ ℚ(z)` is *zero modulo `p`* if `r = f / g` with `f, g ∈ ℤ[z]`,
`g ≢ 0 (mod p)` and `f ≡ 0 (mod p)`. Equivalently, `r` has `p`-adic Gauss norm less than `1`,
i.e. `r` is `p`-integral and its reduction in `𝔽_p(z)` is `0`. -/
def IsZeroModP (p : ℕ) (r : RatFunc ℚ) : Prop :=
  ∃ f g : ℤ[X], g.map (Int.castRingHom (ZMod p)) ≠ 0 ∧ f.map (Int.castRingHom (ZMod p)) = 0 ∧
    r = algebraMap ℚ[X] (RatFunc ℚ) (f.map (Int.castRingHom ℚ)) /
      algebraMap ℚ[X] (RatFunc ℚ) (g.map (Int.castRingHom ℚ))

@[category test, AMS 11]
theorem isZeroModP_zero (p : ℕ) [Fact p.Prime] : IsZeroModP p 0 :=
  ⟨0, 1, by simp, by simp, by simp⟩

@[category test, AMS 11]
theorem not_isZeroModP_one (p : ℕ) : ¬ IsZeroModP p 1 := by
  rintro ⟨f, g, hg, hf, h⟩
  have hg' : g.map (Int.castRingHom ℚ) ≠ 0 := by
    rintro hg'
    simp [hg'] at h
  rw [eq_div_iff (algebraMap_ne_zero hg'), one_mul] at h
  have hfg : f = g := Polynomial.map_injective _ (Int.castRingHom ℚ).injective_int
    (algebraMap_injective ℚ h).symm
  exact hg (hfg ▸ hf)

/-- The linear differential system `Y' = A Y`, for `A` an `n × n` matrix over `ℚ(z)`, has
*`p`-curvature zero modulo `p`*: `A` can be reduced modulo `p` (all its entries are `p`-integral)
and the `p`-curvature matrix `A_p` of the reduction is zero, i.e. `A_p ≡ 0 (mod p)` entrywise.
By a theorem of Cartier, this holds if and only if the reduction modulo `p` of the system has a
full set of solutions in `𝔽_p(z)` (equivalently, of solutions algebraic over `𝔽_p(z)`). -/
def HasPCurvatureZero {n : ℕ} (p : ℕ) (A : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) (RatFunc ℚ)) : Prop :=
  (∀ i j, IsPIntegral p (A i j)) ∧ ∀ i j, IsZeroModP p (higherDerivMatrix A p i j)

end ReductionModP

/- ### Full sets of algebraic solutions -/

section AlgebraicSolutions

variable {F : Type*} [Field F] [Differential F] [CharZero F]

/-- The linear differential system `Y' = A Y`, for `A` an `n × n` matrix over a differential
field `F` of characteristic `0`, has a *full set of algebraic solutions*: there is a fundamental
matrix of solutions, i.e. an invertible `n × n` matrix `Y` with `Y' = A Y`, whose entries lie in
a finite extension `L` of `F` (inside an algebraic closure of `F`). Here `L` carries the unique
derivation extending that of `F`. -/
def HasFullSetOfAlgebraicSolutions {n : ℕ} (A : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) F) : Prop :=
  ∃ (L : IntermediateField F (AlgebraicClosure F)) (_ : FiniteDimensional F L)
    (Y : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) L),
    IsUnit Y ∧ Y.map (·′) = A.map (algebraMap F L) * Y

@[category test, AMS 12]
theorem hasFullSetOfAlgebraicSolutions_zero (n : ℕ) :
    HasFullSetOfAlgebraicSolutions (0 : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) F) :=
  ⟨⊥, inferInstance, 1, isUnit_one, by
    ext i j
    by_cases h : i = j <;> simp [h]⟩

end AlgebraicSolutions

/-- **Grothendieck–Katz $p$-curvature conjecture** (Grothendieck's conjecture, in its essential
case). Let $A$ be an $n \times n$ matrix of rational functions in $\mathbb{Q}(z)$, and consider
the linear differential system $dY/dz = A(z)\,Y$. Let $A_0 = I$ and $A_{k+1} = A_k' + A_k A$, so
that $d^kY/dz^k = A_k Y$ for every solution $Y$.

Suppose that for all but finitely many primes $p$, the system can be reduced modulo $p$ and the
reduced system has $p$-curvature zero, i.e. $A_p \equiv 0 \pmod p$ (equivalently, the reduced
system has a full set of solutions in $\mathbb{F}_p(z)$, or algebraic over $\mathbb{F}_p(z)$).
Then the system has a full set of algebraic solutions: a fundamental matrix
$Y \in \mathrm{GL}_n(L)$ with $Y' = AY$, whose entries lie in a finite extension $L$ of
$\mathbb{Q}(z)$.

Only this sufficiency direction is conjectural; the converse is a classical theorem
(see `grothendieck_katz_p_curvature_conjecture.variants.necessity`). -/
@[category research open, AMS 11 12 14]
theorem grothendieck_katz_p_curvature_conjecture {n : ℕ}
    (A : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) (RatFunc ℚ))
    (hA : ∀ᶠ p in Filter.cofinite, p.Prime → HasPCurvatureZero p A) :
    HasFullSetOfAlgebraicSolutions A := by
  sorry

/-- The classical converse of the Grothendieck–Katz $p$-curvature conjecture (Cartier, Katz):
if the linear differential system $dY/dz = A(z)\,Y$ with $A \in M_n(\mathbb{Q}(z))$ has a full
set of algebraic solutions, then for all but finitely many primes $p$ its reduction modulo $p$ is
defined and has $p$-curvature zero, i.e. $A_p \equiv 0 \pmod p$. -/
@[category research solved, AMS 11 12 14]
theorem grothendieck_katz_p_curvature_conjecture.variants.necessity {n : ℕ}
    (A : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) (RatFunc ℚ)) (hA : HasFullSetOfAlgebraicSolutions A) :
    ∀ᶠ p in Filter.cofinite, p.Prime → HasPCurvatureZero p A := by
  sorry

end GrothendieckKatzPCurvatureConjecture
attempts.decomposition_objections: None of substance. The table is right that the Katz Galois-group version is a subordinate equivalent reformulation; I note only that it cannot currently be stated faithfully for lack of algebraic-group primitives, which is a Mathlib gap rather than a table error.
modeling_decisions: The list-page entry is terse, so the statement was taken from the article's 'essential case' (rational-function matrix A over ℚ(z), rational coefficients), as the notes prescribe; the number-field/étale-cover version (Chambert-Loir's Conj.) is treated as the same question and not stated separately.

ℚ(z) is modelled as `RatFunc ℚ`. Mathlib has no derivation on RatFunc, so `d/dz` is defined by the quotient rule on num/denom, proven to satisfy the quotient rule for every representation p/q (`ratFuncDerivative_div`), additivity and Leibniz, and packaged as a `Differential (RatFunc K)` instance; `deriv_algebraMap_polynomial`, `deriv_X`, `deriv_C` check it agrees with `Polynomial.derivative`. This instance is reusable and would belong in FormalConjecturesForMathlib in a real PR.

The mod-p condition is encoded via the matrices A_k of Chambert-Loir (A_0 = I, A_{k+1} = A_k' + A_k A, column convention dY/dz = A Y matching Wikipedia's dv/dz = A(z)v): `HasPCurvatureZero p A` := all entries of A are p-integral (A can be reduced mod p) ∧ all entries of A_p are ≡ 0 mod p. By Cartier's theorem (quoted in Chambert-Loir) this is exactly 'the reduction mod p has a full set of solutions in 𝔽_p(z) / algebraic over 𝔽_p(z)'. Including the reducibility clause is harmless under the cofinite quantifier and matches the source's 'si l'on peut réduire A modulo p'.

`IsPIntegral p r` (r = f/g, f,g ∈ ℤ[z], g ≢ 0 mod p) and `IsZeroModP p r` (additionally f ≡ 0 mod p) are elementary encodings of 'p-adic Gauss norm ≤ 1' and '< 1'; by Gauss's lemma they are representation-independent and equal to 'reducible mod p' and 'reduces to 0 in 𝔽_p(z)'. Congruences of ℤ[z] are expressed via `Polynomial.map (Int.castRingHom (ZMod p))`.
'Almost all primes' is `∀ᶠ p in Filter.cofinite, p.Prime → …`, i.e. all but finitely many primes (cofinite, not merely infinitely many), as the notes require.

'Full set of algebraic solutions' = a fundamental matrix: `∃ L : IntermediateField F (AlgebraicClosure F)` finite-dimensional over F, `∃ Y : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) L`, `IsUnit Y ∧ Y.map (·′) = A.map (algebraMap F L) * Y`. The derivation on L is Mathlib's `Differential.instSubtypeMemIntermediateFieldOfFiniteDimensional` (verified by #synth), the unique extension of the derivation of F (`uniqueDifferentialAlgebraFiniteDimensional`). Any finite set of algebraic elements lies in such an L, so this is equivalent to 'n independent solutions algebraic over ℚ(z)'. The predicate is stated for a general differential field F of characteristic 0 (instantiated at F = RatFunc ℚ) to avoid a RatFunc-specific typeclass-search blow-up.

Only the sufficiency direction is the open conjecture (`research open`). The classical necessity (Cartier/Katz 1970–72) is added as `grothendieck_katz_p_curvature_conjecture.variants.necessity` tagged `research solved` with `sorry`, both to document that only one direction is conjectural and to exercise the definitions; a reviewer should confirm they want this extra declaration.
Index type is `Fin n` (n×n matrices); n = 0 makes both hypothesis and conclusion trivially true, which is consistent.

namespace GrothendieckKatzPCurvatureConjecture

/-- The formal derivative of a rational function in one variable. -/
noncomputable def ratFuncDerivative {K : Type*} [Field K] (f : RatFunc K) : RatFunc K :=
  RatFunc.mk
    (f.num.derivative * f.denom - f.num * f.denom.derivative)
    (f.denom ^ 2)

/--
`IsReduction p f fₚ` means that the rational functions `f` over $\mathbb{Q}$ and `fₚ`
over $\mathbb{F}_p$ admit the same numerator and denominator with integer coefficients,
with the denominator remaining nonzero after reduction modulo $p$.
-/
def IsReduction (p : ℕ) [Fact p.Prime] (f : RatFunc ℚ) (fₚ : RatFunc (ZMod p)) : Prop :=
  ∃ a b : Polynomial ℤ,
    b.map (Int.castRingHom ℚ) ≠ 0 ∧
    b.map (Int.castRingHom (ZMod p)) ≠ 0 ∧
    f = RatFunc.mk (a.map (Int.castRingHom ℚ)) (b.map (Int.castRingHom ℚ)) ∧
    fₚ = RatFunc.mk (a.map (Int.castRingHom (ZMod p))) (b.map (Int.castRingHom (ZMod p)))

/-- Entrywise reduction modulo `p` of a matrix of rational functions. -/
def IsMatrixReduction {n p : ℕ} [Fact p.Prime]
    (A : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) (RatFunc ℚ))
    (Aₚ : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) (RatFunc (ZMod p))) : Prop :=
  ∀ i j, IsReduction p (A i j) (Aₚ i j)

/--
The matrices $G_r$ determined by $G_0=I$ and $G_{r+1}=G_r'+G_rA$.
For a system $Y'=AY$ in characteristic $p$, its $p$-curvature vanishes exactly when
$G_p=0$.
-/
noncomputable def iteratedConnectionMatrix {K : Type*} [Field K] {n : ℕ}
    (A : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) (RatFunc K)) :
    ℕ → Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) (RatFunc K)
  | 0 => 1
  | r + 1 => (iteratedConnectionMatrix A r).map ratFuncDerivative +
      iteratedConnectionMatrix A r * A

/-- The system `Y' = A Y` has zero `p`-curvature after reduction modulo the prime `p`. -/
def HasZeroPCurvatureReduction {n : ℕ}
    (A : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) (RatFunc ℚ)) (p : ℕ) (hp : p.Prime) : Prop :=
  letI : Fact p.Prime := ⟨hp⟩
  ∃ Aₚ : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) (RatFunc (ZMod p)),
    IsMatrixReduction A Aₚ ∧ iteratedConnectionMatrix Aₚ p = 0

/--
The system `Y' = A Y` has a fundamental matrix in an algebraic differential field
extension of $\mathbb{Q}(z)$. The displayed compatibility says that the derivation on the
extension restricts to the usual derivative with respect to $z$.
-/
def HasFullSetOfAlgebraicSolutions {n : ℕ}
    (A : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) (RatFunc ℚ)) : Prop :=
  ∃ (L : Type) (_ : Field L) (_ : Algebra ℚ L) (_ : Algebra (RatFunc ℚ) L)
      (_ : IsScalarTower ℚ (RatFunc ℚ) L),
    Algebra.IsAlgebraic (RatFunc ℚ) L ∧
    ∃ D : Derivation ℚ L L,
      (∀ f : RatFunc ℚ,
        D (algebraMap (RatFunc ℚ) L f) =
          algebraMap (RatFunc ℚ) L (ratFuncDerivative f)) ∧
      ∃ Y : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) L,
        IsUnit Y ∧
        ∀ i j, D (Y i j) = ∑ k, algebraMap (RatFunc ℚ) L (A i k) * Y k j

/--
**Grothendieck–Katz p-curvature conjecture (essential case).**

Let $n>0$ and let $A$ be an $n\times n$ matrix over $\mathbb{Q}(z)$. If, for all but
finitely many primes $p$, the reduction modulo $p$ of the system $Y'=AY$ is defined and
has zero $p$-curvature (equivalently, it has a full set of solutions in
$\mathbb{F}_p(z)$), then the original system has a fundamental matrix whose entries are
algebraic over $\mathbb{Q}(z)$.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 12 34]
theorem grothendieck_katz_p_curvature_conjecture (n : ℕ) (hn : 0 < n)
    (A : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) (RatFunc ℚ))
    (hA : ∀ᶠ p in Filter.cofinite, ∀ hp : p.Prime, HasZeroPCurvatureReduction A p hp) :
    HasFullSetOfAlgebraicSolutions A := by

end GrothendieckKatzPCurvatureConjecture

namespace GrothendieckKatzPCurvatureConjecture

/-- An integral numerator-denominator presentation of a matrix over a rational function field. -/
structure IntegralPresentation (n : ℕ) where
  numerator : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) (Polynomial ℤ)
  denominator : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) (Polynomial ℤ)
  denominator_ne_zero : ∀ i j, denominator i j ≠ 0

/-- The matrix over `RatFunc K` obtained from an integral presentation by casting coefficients. -/
noncomputable def IntegralPresentation.matrix {n : ℕ} (S : IntegralPresentation n)
    (K : Type*) [Field K] : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) (RatFunc K) :=
  fun i j ↦ RatFunc.mk ((S.numerator i j).map (Int.castRingHom K))
    ((S.denominator i j).map (Int.castRingHom K))

/-- An integral presentation has good reduction in characteristic `p` when none of its displayed
entrywise denominators becomes the zero polynomial. -/
def IntegralPresentation.IsGoodAt {n : ℕ} (S : IntegralPresentation n) (p : Nat.Primes) : Prop :=
  ∀ i j, (S.denominator i j).map (Int.castRingHom (ZMod p)) ≠ 0

/-- `g` is the formal derivative of the rational function `f`. This relational formulation uses
an arbitrary polynomial fraction representing `f` and applies the quotient rule. -/
def IsRatFuncDerivative {K : Type*} [Field K] (f g : RatFunc K) : Prop :=
  ∃ P Q : Polynomial K, Q ≠ 0 ∧ f = RatFunc.mk P Q ∧
    g = RatFunc.mk (P.derivative * Q - P * Q.derivative) (Q ^ 2)

/-- A full set of solutions of `Y' = A Y` over `K(x)`, encoded by an invertible fundamental
matrix. -/
def HasFundamentalMatrix {n : ℕ} {K : Type*} [Field K]
    (A : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) (RatFunc K)) : Prop :=
  ∃ Y Y' : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) (RatFunc K), Matrix.det Y ≠ 0 ∧
    (∀ i j, IsRatFuncDerivative (Y i j) (Y' i j)) ∧ Y' = A * Y

/-- A derivation on an extension of `K(x)` is the standard `d/dx` when it obeys the quotient rule
on the embedded rational function field. -/
def IsStandardExtensionDerivation (K L : Type*) [Field K] [Field L] [Algebra K L]
    [Algebra (RatFunc K) L] (D : Derivation K L L) : Prop :=
  ∀ (P Q : Polynomial K), Q ≠ 0 →
    D (algebraMap (RatFunc K) L (RatFunc.mk P Q)) =
      algebraMap (RatFunc K) L
        (RatFunc.mk (P.derivative * Q - P * Q.derivative) (Q ^ 2))

/-- The reduced system associated to `S` has a fundamental matrix over `𝔽_p(x)`. The local
instance records that a prime modulus gives a field. -/
def HasGoodReductionSolutionAt {n : ℕ} (S : IntegralPresentation n) (p : Nat.Primes) : Prop :=
  letI : Fact (Nat.Prime p) := ⟨p.prop⟩
  S.IsGoodAt p ∧ HasFundamentalMatrix (S.matrix (ZMod p))

/-- The system `Y' = A Y` has a full set of solutions algebraic over `ℚ(x)`. -/
def HasAlgebraicFundamentalMatrix {n : ℕ}
    (A : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) (RatFunc ℚ)) : Prop :=
  ∃ (L : Type) (_ : Field L) (_ : Algebra ℚ L) (_ : Algebra (RatFunc ℚ) L)
      (_ : IsScalarTower ℚ (RatFunc ℚ) L) (_ : Algebra.IsAlgebraic (RatFunc ℚ) L)
      (D : Derivation ℚ L L) (Y : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) L),
    IsStandardExtensionDerivation ℚ L D ∧ Matrix.det Y ≠ 0 ∧
      Matrix.map Y D = Matrix.map A (algebraMap (RatFunc ℚ) L) * Y

Grothendieck's p-curvature conjecture in its essential matrix form. Let
$Y' = A(x)Y$ be a linear system over $\mathbb{Q}(x)$. If, for all but finitely many
primes $p$, an integral presentation of $A$ has good reduction and the reduced system
has an invertible fundamental matrix over $\mathbb{F}_p(x)$ (equivalently, its
$p$-curvature vanishes), then the original system has an invertible fundamental matrix
whose entries are algebraic over $\mathbb{Q}(x)$.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 12 34]
theorem grothendieck_katz_p_curvature_conjecture {n : ℕ} (S : IntegralPresentation n)
    (h : ∀ᶠ p : Nat.Primes in Filter.cofinite, HasGoodReductionSolutionAt S p) :
    HasAlgebraicFundamentalMatrix (S.matrix ℚ) := by

end GrothendieckKatzPCurvatureConjecture

/-!
# Grothendieck–Katz $p$-curvature conjecture

A local–global principle for linear ordinary differential equations, conjectured by
Grothendieck around 1969 and first published by Katz.

Consider a linear differential system
$$\frac{dY}{dz} = A(z)\,Y, \qquad A(z) \in M_n(\mathbb{Q}(z)).$$
Define matrices $A_k \in M_n(\mathbb{Q}(z))$ by $A_0 = I$ and $A_{k+1} = A_k' + A_k A$, so that
any solution satisfies $Y^{(k)} = A_k Y$. For all but finitely many primes $p$ the matrix $A$
can be reduced modulo $p$, and (Cartier) the reduced system $dY/dz = \bar A\,Y$ over
$\mathbb{F}_p(z)$ has a full set of solutions in $\mathbb{F}_p(z)$ (equivalently, of solutions
algebraic over $\mathbb{F}_p(z)$) if and only if the *$p$-curvature* $A_p$ is zero modulo $p$.

If the original system has a full set of solutions algebraic over $\mathbb{Q}(z)$, then this
necessary condition holds for almost all $p$. **Grothendieck's conjecture** is that the
condition is also sufficient: if $A_p \equiv 0 \pmod p$ for all but finitely many primes $p$,
then $dY/dz = AY$ has a fundamental matrix of solutions whose entries are algebraic over
$\mathbb{Q}(z)$. The general case (connections on smooth varieties over number fields) reduces
to this one.

Katz's equivalent reformulation (Katz 1982, Conjecture 9.2), which describes the Lie algebra of
the generic differential Galois group of the equation as the smallest algebraic Lie subalgebra
of $\mathfrak{gl}_n$ whose reduction modulo $p$ contains the $p$-curvature for almost all $p$,
is not stated here: Mathlib has neither linear algebraic groups (with their Lie algebras) nor
the differential Galois group.

- [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grothendieck%E2%80%93Katz_p-curvature_conjecture)
- N. M. Katz, *Algebraic solutions of differential equations (p-curvature and the Hodge
  filtration)*, Invent. Math. 18 (1972), 1–118.
- N. M. Katz, *A conjecture in the arithmetic theory of differential equations*,
  Bull. Soc. Math. France 110 (1982), 203–239.
- A. Chambert-Loir, *Théorèmes d'algébrisation en géométrie diophantienne*, Séminaire Bourbaki

/- ### The derivation `d/dX` on the field of rational functions `K(X)`

Mathlib has no derivation on `RatFunc K`. We construct `d/dX` by extending
`P ↦ P(X + ε) = P(X) + P'(X) ε ∈ K(X)[ε]` (dual numbers) from `K[X]` to its fraction field
`K(X)` and taking the `ε`-coefficient. -/

section RatFuncDerivative

variable {K : Type*} [Field K]

@[category API, AMS 12]
lemma eval₂_algebraMap_X_ratFunc (Q : K[X]) :
    eval₂ (algebraMap K (RatFunc K)) RatFunc.X Q = algebraMap K[X] (RatFunc K) Q := by
  simpa using eval₂_algebraMap_X Q (IsScalarTower.toAlgHom K K[X] (RatFunc K))

/-- The ring homomorphism `K[X] → K(X)[ε]`, `P ↦ P(X + ε) = P(X) + P'(X) ε`. -/
noncomputable def ratFuncDerivAux₀ : K[X] →+* DualNumber (RatFunc K) :=
  eval₂RingHom ((inlHom (RatFunc K) (RatFunc K)).comp (algebraMap K (RatFunc K)))
    (inl RatFunc.X + DualNumber.eps)

@[category API, AMS 12]
lemma ratFuncDerivAux₀_apply (P : K[X]) :
    ratFuncDerivAux₀ P = inl (algebraMap K[X] (RatFunc K) P) +
      inr (algebraMap K[X] (RatFunc K) (derivative P)) := by
  have key : ∀ Q : K[X], eval₂ ((inlHom (RatFunc K) (RatFunc K)).comp (algebraMap K (RatFunc K)))
      (inl RatFunc.X) Q = inl (algebraMap K[X] (RatFunc K) Q) := by
    intro Q
    have := hom_eval₂ Q (algebraMap K (RatFunc K)) (inlHom (RatFunc K) (RatFunc K)) RatFunc.X
    rw [inlHom_apply, eval₂_algebraMap_X_ratFunc, inlHom_apply] at this
    exact this.symm
  simp only [ratFuncDerivAux₀, coe_eval₂RingHom]
  rw [eval₂_eq_eval_map, eval_add_of_sq_eq_zero _ _ _ (by simp [sq]), derivative_map,
    ← eval₂_eq_eval_map, ← eval₂_eq_eval_map, key, key, DualNumber.eps, inl_mul_inr, smul_eq_mul,
    mul_one]

@[category API, AMS 12]
lemma isUnit_ratFuncDerivAux₀ (Q : nonZeroDivisors K[X]) :
    IsUnit (ratFuncDerivAux₀ (Q : K[X])) := by
  rw [isUnit_iff_isUnit_fst, ratFuncDerivAux₀_apply, fst_add, fst_inl, fst_inr, add_zero,
    isUnit_iff_ne_zero]
  exact RatFunc.algebraMap_ne_zero (nonZeroDivisors.ne_zero Q.2)

/-- The ring homomorphism `K(X) → K(X)[ε]`, `f ↦ f + f' ε`. -/
noncomputable def ratFuncDerivAux : RatFunc K →+* DualNumber (RatFunc K) :=
  IsLocalization.lift (M := nonZeroDivisors K[X]) isUnit_ratFuncDerivAux₀

@[category API, AMS 12]
lemma ratFuncDerivAux_algebraMap (P : K[X]) :
    ratFuncDerivAux (algebraMap K[X] (RatFunc K) P) = inl (algebraMap K[X] (RatFunc K) P) +
      inr (algebraMap K[X] (RatFunc K) (derivative P)) := by
  rw [ratFuncDerivAux, IsLocalization.lift_eq, ratFuncDerivAux₀_apply]

/-- The ring homomorphism `f ↦ f + f' ε` lifts the identity of `K(X)`. -/
@[category API, AMS 12]
lemma fst_ratFuncDerivAux (f : RatFunc K) : fst (ratFuncDerivAux f) = f := by
  have : ((fstHom K (RatFunc K) (RatFunc K) : DualNumber (RatFunc K) →ₐ[K] RatFunc K) :
      DualNumber (RatFunc K) →+* RatFunc K).comp ratFuncDerivAux = RingHom.id _ := by
    apply IsLocalization.ringHom_ext (nonZeroDivisors K[X])
    refine Polynomial.ringHom_ext (fun a => ?_) ?_ <;>
      simp only [RingHom.comp_apply, ratFuncDerivAux_algebraMap] <;> simp
  exact RingHom.congr_fun this f

@[category API, AMS 12]
lemma snd_ratFuncDerivAux_add (a b : RatFunc K) :
    (snd (ratFuncDerivAux (a + b)) : RatFunc K) =
      snd (ratFuncDerivAux a) + snd (ratFuncDerivAux b) := by
  rw [RingHom.map_add ratFuncDerivAux a b, snd_add]

@[category API, AMS 12]
lemma snd_ratFuncDerivAux_mul (a b : RatFunc K) :
    (snd (ratFuncDerivAux (a * b)) : RatFunc K) =
      a * snd (ratFuncDerivAux b) + b * snd (ratFuncDerivAux a) := by
  rw [RingHom.map_mul ratFuncDerivAux a b, DualNumber.snd_mul, fst_ratFuncDerivAux,
    fst_ratFuncDerivAux, mul_comm (snd _) b]

@[category API, AMS 12]
lemma snd_ratFuncDerivAux_one : (snd (ratFuncDerivAux (1 : RatFunc K)) : RatFunc K) = 0 := by
  rw [RingHom.map_one ratFuncDerivAux, snd_one]

@[category API, AMS 12]
lemma snd_ratFuncDerivAux_intCast (z : ℤ) :
    (snd (ratFuncDerivAux (z : RatFunc K)) : RatFunc K) = 0 := by
  rw [← map_intCast (algebraMap K[X] (RatFunc K)), ratFuncDerivAux_algebraMap, snd_add, snd_inl,
    snd_inr, zero_add, derivative_intCast, map_zero]

/-- The derivation `d/dX` on the field of rational functions `K(X)`. -/
noncomputable def ratFuncDerivative : Derivation ℤ (RatFunc K) (RatFunc K) where
  toFun f := snd (ratFuncDerivAux f)
  map_add' := snd_ratFuncDerivAux_add
  map_smul' z a := by
    simp only [Algebra.smul_def, eq_intCast, Int.cast_id, zsmul_eq_mul]
    rw [snd_ratFuncDerivAux_mul, snd_ratFuncDerivAux_intCast, mul_zero, add_zero]
  map_one_eq_zero' := snd_ratFuncDerivAux_one
  leibniz' a b := by
    simp only [smul_eq_mul]
    exact snd_ratFuncDerivAux_mul a b

/-- On polynomials, `ratFuncDerivative` is the usual derivative of polynomials. -/
@[category API, AMS 12]
lemma ratFuncDerivative_algebraMap (P : K[X]) :
    ratFuncDerivative (algebraMap K[X] (RatFunc K) P) =
      algebraMap K[X] (RatFunc K) (derivative P) := by
  change snd (ratFuncDerivAux _) = _
  rw [ratFuncDerivAux_algebraMap, snd_add, snd_inl, snd_inr, zero_add]

/-- `dX/dX = 1`. -/
@[category API, AMS 12]
lemma ratFuncDerivative_X : ratFuncDerivative (RatFunc.X : RatFunc K) = 1 := by
  rw [← RatFunc.algebraMap_X, ratFuncDerivative_algebraMap]
  simp

/-- Constants have derivative `0`. -/
@[category API, AMS 12]
lemma ratFuncDerivative_C (c : K) : ratFuncDerivative (algebraMap K (RatFunc K) c) = 0 := by
  rw [RatFunc.algebraMap_eq_C, ← RatFunc.algebraMap_C, ratFuncDerivative_algebraMap]
  simp

/-- The quotient rule. -/
@[category API, AMS 12]
lemma ratFuncDerivative_div (f g : RatFunc K) :
    ratFuncDerivative (f / g) =
      (ratFuncDerivative f * g - f * ratFuncDerivative g) / g ^ 2 := by
  by_cases hg : g = 0
  · simp [hg]
  · rw [Derivation.leibniz_div]
    simp only [smul_eq_mul]
    field_simp

end RatFuncDerivative

/- ### Reduction modulo `p` of rational functions over `ℚ` -/

section ReductionModP

/-- A rational function `f ∈ ℚ(z)` is *`p`-integral* if `f = P(z)/Q(z)` with
`P, Q ∈ ℤ[z]` and `Q ≢ 0 (mod p)`. Such an `f` can be reduced modulo `p`, to the element
`P̄/Q̄` of `𝔽_p(z)`. -/
def IsPIntegral (p : ℕ) (f : RatFunc ℚ) : Prop :=
  ∃ P Q : ℤ[X], Q.map (Int.castRingHom (ZMod p)) ≠ 0 ∧
    f = aeval RatFunc.X P / aeval RatFunc.X Q

/-- A rational function `f ∈ ℚ(z)` is *zero modulo `p`* if `f = P(z)/Q(z)` with
`P, Q ∈ ℤ[z]`, `Q ≢ 0 (mod p)` and `P ≡ 0 (mod p)`, i.e. `f` is `p`-integral and its reduction
modulo `p` is `0 ∈ 𝔽_p(z)`. -/
def IsZeroModP (p : ℕ) (f : RatFunc ℚ) : Prop :=
  ∃ P Q : ℤ[X], Q.map (Int.castRingHom (ZMod p)) ≠ 0 ∧ P.map (Int.castRingHom (ZMod p)) = 0 ∧
    f = aeval RatFunc.X P / aeval RatFunc.X Q

/-- Evaluating `P ∈ ℤ[X]` at `z ∈ ℚ(z)` is the inclusion `ℤ[z] ⊆ ℚ[z] ⊆ ℚ(z)`. -/
@[category API, AMS 12]
lemma aeval_X_eq (P : ℤ[X]) :
    aeval (RatFunc.X : RatFunc ℚ) P =
      algebraMap ℚ[X] (RatFunc ℚ) (P.map (Int.castRingHom ℚ)) := by
  rw [← RatFunc.algebraMap_X, ← IsScalarTower.coe_toAlgHom' ℤ ℚ[X] (RatFunc ℚ),
    aeval_algHom_apply, aeval_X_left_eq_map, IsScalarTower.coe_toAlgHom', algebraMap_int_eq]

/-- The inclusion `ℤ[z] → ℚ(z)` is injective. -/
@[category API, AMS 12]
lemma aeval_X_injective :
    Function.Injective (aeval (RatFunc.X : RatFunc ℚ) : ℤ[X] → RatFunc ℚ) := by
  intro P Q h
  rw [aeval_X_eq, aeval_X_eq] at h
  exact Polynomial.map_injective _ (Int.castRingHom ℚ).injective_int
    (RatFunc.algebraMap_injective ℚ h)

/-- The integer `p` is zero modulo `p`. -/
@[category test, AMS 11 12]
lemma isZeroModP_natCast (p : ℕ) [Fact p.Prime] : IsZeroModP p (p : RatFunc ℚ) := by
  refine ⟨C (p : ℤ), 1, by simp, by simp, by simp⟩

/-- The constant `1` is not zero modulo `p`. -/
@[category test, AMS 11 12]
lemma not_isZeroModP_one (p : ℕ) : ¬ IsZeroModP p (1 : RatFunc ℚ) := by
  rintro ⟨P, Q, hQ, hP, h⟩
  have hQ' : aeval (RatFunc.X : RatFunc ℚ) Q ≠ 0 := by
    intro h0
    have hQ0 : Q = 0 := aeval_X_injective (by rw [h0, map_zero])
    exact hQ (by rw [hQ0, Polynomial.map_zero])
  rw [eq_comm, div_eq_one_iff_eq hQ'] at h
  have hPQ := aeval_X_injective h
  subst hPQ
  exact hQ hP

end ReductionModP

/- ### The linear differential system `Y' = A Y` -/

section Statement

variable {n : ℕ}

/-- The matrices `A_k` attached to the system `Y' = A Y`: `A₀ = 1` and `A_{k+1} = A_k' + A_k A`,
where `'` is entrywise `d/dz`. They satisfy `Y⁽ᵏ⁾ = A_k Y` for every solution `Y`. For a prime
`p`, the matrix `A_p` reduced modulo `p` is, up to sign, the *`p`-curvature* of the reduced
system. -/
noncomputable def higherDerivativeMatrix (A : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) (RatFunc ℚ)) :
    ℕ → Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) (RatFunc ℚ)
  | 0 => 1
  | k + 1 => (higherDerivativeMatrix A k).map ratFuncDerivative + higherDerivativeMatrix A k * A

/-- The system `Y' = A Y` *has zero `p`-curvature*: `A` can be reduced modulo `p` and the
`p`-curvature matrix `A_p` is zero modulo `p`. By Cartier's theorem, this holds if and only if
the system reduced modulo `p` has a full set of solutions in `𝔽_p(z)` (equivalently, a full set
of solutions algebraic over `𝔽_p(z)`). -/
def HasZeroPCurvatureModP (A : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) (RatFunc ℚ)) (p : ℕ) : Prop :=
  (∀ i j, IsPIntegral p (A i j)) ∧ ∀ i j, IsZeroModP p (higherDerivativeMatrix A p i j)

/-- The system `Y' = A Y` over `ℚ(z)` *has a full set of algebraic solutions*: there are a
finite extension `L` of `ℚ(z)`, a derivation `D` of `L` extending `d/dz` (it is then the unique
such derivation), and an invertible matrix `Y ∈ GL_n(L)`, the fundamental matrix, with
`D Y = A Y`. In other words, the system has `n` linearly independent solutions whose entries are
algebraic functions over `ℚ(z)`. -/
def HasFullSetOfAlgebraicSolutions (A : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) (RatFunc ℚ)) : Prop :=
  ∃ (L : Type) (_ : Field L) (_ : Algebra (RatFunc ℚ) L) (_ : FiniteDimensional (RatFunc ℚ) L)
    (D : Derivation ℤ L L),
    (∀ f, D (algebraMap (RatFunc ℚ) L f) = algebraMap (RatFunc ℚ) L (ratFuncDerivative f)) ∧
    ∃ Y : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) L, IsUnit Y ∧ Y.map D = A.map (algebraMap (RatFunc ℚ) L) * Y

/-- `A₁ = A`. -/
@[category API, AMS 12]
lemma higherDerivativeMatrix_one (A : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) (RatFunc ℚ)) :
    higherDerivativeMatrix A 1 = A := by
  have : (1 : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) (RatFunc ℚ)).map ratFuncDerivative = 0 := by
    ext i j
    by_cases h : i = j <;> simp [h]
  simp [higherDerivativeMatrix, this]

/-- The trivial system `Y' = 0` has zero `p`-curvature for every prime `p`. -/
@[category test, AMS 11 12]
lemma hasZeroPCurvatureModP_zero (p : ℕ) [hp : Fact p.Prime] :
    HasZeroPCurvatureModP (0 : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) (RatFunc ℚ)) p := by
  have h0 : ∀ k, higherDerivativeMatrix (0 : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) (RatFunc ℚ)) (k + 1) = 0 := by
    intro k
    induction k with
    | zero => simp [higherDerivativeMatrix_one]
    | succ k ih =>
      rw [higherDerivativeMatrix, ih]
      ext i j
      simp
  refine ⟨fun i j => ⟨0, 1, by simp, by simp⟩, fun i j => ⟨0, 1, by simp, by simp, ?_⟩⟩
  obtain ⟨k, rfl⟩ := Nat.exists_eq_succ_of_ne_zero hp.out.ne_zero
  simp [h0]

/-- The trivial system `Y' = 0` has a full set of algebraic (indeed rational) solutions. -/
@[category test, AMS 12]
lemma hasFullSetOfAlgebraicSolutions_zero :
    HasFullSetOfAlgebraicSolutions (0 : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) (RatFunc ℚ)) := by
  -- Mathlib has two (propositionally equal, non-defeq) instances of `Algebra ℤ (RatFunc ℚ)`, so
  -- `ratFuncDerivative` has to be repackaged as a derivation for the instance used in `L`.
  refine ⟨RatFunc ℚ, inferInstance, inferInstance, inferInstance,
    @Derivation.mk ℤ (RatFunc ℚ) (RatFunc ℚ) _ _ _ (Ring.toIntAlgebra _) _ _
      (@LinearMap.mk ℤ ℤ _ _ (RingHom.id ℤ) (RatFunc ℚ) (RatFunc ℚ) _ _ _ _
        ⟨fun f => ratFuncDerivative f, ?_⟩ ?_) ?_ ?_, fun f => rfl, 1, isUnit_one, ?_⟩
  · intro a b
    exact ratFuncDerivative.map_add a b
  · intro z a
    have h := (ratFuncDerivative (K := ℚ)).map_smul z a
    rw [Algebra.smul_def, eq_intCast, zsmul_eq_mul] at h
    simp only [RingHom.id_apply, zsmul_eq_mul]
    exact h
  · exact ratFuncDerivative.map_one_eq_zero
  · intro a b
    exact ratFuncDerivative.leibniz a b
  · ext i j
    by_cases h : i = j <;> simp [h]

/-- **Grothendieck–Katz $p$-curvature conjecture** (Grothendieck's conjecture, essential case).
Let $A \in M_n(\mathbb{Q}(z))$. Suppose that for all but finitely many primes $p$, the system
$dY/dz = A\,Y$ can be reduced modulo $p$ and its $p$-curvature $A_p$ vanishes modulo $p$
(equivalently, the reduced system has a full set of solutions in $\mathbb{F}_p(z)$). Then the
system $dY/dz = A\,Y$ has a full set of solutions algebraic over $\mathbb{Q}(z)$, i.e. a
fundamental matrix $Y \in GL_n(L)$ for some finite extension $L$ of $\mathbb{Q}(z)$.

The converse (necessity of the mod $p$ condition) is a classical theorem; only this
sufficiency direction is conjectural. -/
@[category research open, AMS 11 12 14 34]
theorem grothendieck_katz_p_curvature_conjecture (A : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) (RatFunc ℚ))
    (hA : ∀ᶠ p in Filter.cofinite, p.Prime → HasZeroPCurvatureModP A p) :
    HasFullSetOfAlgebraicSolutions A := by
  sorry

end Statement

end GrothendieckKatzPCurvatureConjecture

Katz's reformulation needs (a) the generic (Tannakian) differential Galois group Gal(M) ⊆ GL(M) of a connection over ℚ(x) and its Lie algebra, (b) the notion of an algebraic Lie subalgebra of gl_n over a field (Lie algebra of a Zariski-closed subgroup of GL_n), and (c) reduction modulo p of such Lie subalgebras together with 'contains ψ_p for almost all p'. Mathlib and FormalConjecturesForMathlib have no linear algebraic groups over a field, no Lie algebra of an algebraic group, no differential Galois theory / Picard–Vessiot or Tannakian machinery. Reconstructing all of this bespoke (ideals of MvPolynomial rings plus dual-number tangent spaces, tensor constructions with induced connections including direct sums and subquotients, lattices and reductions) would be a large, fidelity-risky development, so the slot is omitted rather than stated unfaithfully.

/-!
# Grothendieck–Katz p-curvature conjecture

*Reference:* [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grothendieck%E2%80%93Katz_p-curvature_conjecture)
-/

namespace GrothendieckKatzPCurvatureConjecture

open Filter

/--
A rational function `g` over `ZMod p` is a good reduction modulo `p` of a rational
function `f` over `ℚ` if they admit the same quotient presentation by integer polynomials,
and the denominator remains nonzero modulo `p`.
-/
def IsRatFuncReduction (p : Nat.Primes) (f : RatFunc ℚ) (g : RatFunc (ZMod p)) : Prop :=
  letI : Fact (Nat.Prime p) := ⟨p.property⟩
  ∃ P Q : Polynomial ℤ,
    Q.map (Int.castRingHom (ZMod p)) ≠ 0 ∧
    f = RatFunc.mk (P.map (Int.castRingHom ℚ)) (Q.map (Int.castRingHom ℚ)) ∧
    g = RatFunc.mk (P.map (Int.castRingHom (ZMod p))) (Q.map (Int.castRingHom (ZMod p)))

/--
The matrix `B` is a good reduction modulo `p` of `A` when this holds entrywise.
-/
def IsMatrixReduction {n : ℕ} (p : Nat.Primes) (A : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) (RatFunc ℚ))
    (B : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) (RatFunc (ZMod p))) : Prop :=
  ∀ i j, IsRatFuncReduction p (A i j) (B i j)

/--
The system $dY/dz=B Y$ has a full set of solutions in $\mathbb F_p(z)$ if it has an
invertible fundamental matrix over `RatFunc (ZMod p)`. The derivation `D` is the usual
$d/dz$, characterized by being linear over `ZMod p` and satisfying `D RatFunc.X = 1`.
-/
def HasFullSetRationalSolutions {n : ℕ} (p : Nat.Primes)
    (B : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) (RatFunc (ZMod p))) : Prop :=
  letI : Fact (Nat.Prime p) := ⟨p.property⟩
  ∃ (D : Derivation (ZMod p) (RatFunc (ZMod p)) (RatFunc (ZMod p)))
      (Y : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) (RatFunc (ZMod p))),
    D RatFunc.X = 1 ∧ Y.det ≠ 0 ∧
      ∀ i j, D (Y i j) = ∑ k, B i k * Y k j

/--
The system $dY/dz=A Y$ has a full set of solutions algebraic over $\mathbb Q(z)$ if it
has an invertible fundamental matrix in an algebraic closure of `RatFunc ℚ`. The
derivation extends $d/dz$, as expressed by its value on `RatFunc.X`.
-/
noncomputable def HasFullSetAlgebraicSolutions {n : ℕ}
    (A : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) (RatFunc ℚ)) : Prop :=
  let K := AlgebraicClosure (RatFunc ℚ)
  ∃ (D : Derivation ℚ K K) (Y : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) K),
    D (algebraMap (RatFunc ℚ) K RatFunc.X) = 1 ∧ Y.det ≠ 0 ∧
      ∀ i j, D (Y i j) = ∑ k, algebraMap (RatFunc ℚ) K (A i k) * Y k j

/--
**Grothendieck–Katz p-curvature conjecture (essential case).**

Let $A$ be an $n\times n$ matrix over $\mathbb Q(z)$. If, for all but finitely many
primes $p$, the system has a good reduction modulo $p$ with a full fundamental matrix
over $\mathbb F_p(z)$ (equivalently, its $p$-curvature is zero), then the original
system has a full fundamental matrix whose entries are algebraic over $\mathbb Q(z)$.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 12 34]
theorem grothendieck_katz_p_curvature_conjecture {n : ℕ}
    (A : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) (RatFunc ℚ))
    (hA : ∀ᶠ p : Nat.Primes in cofinite,
      ∃ B, IsMatrixReduction p A B ∧ HasFullSetRationalSolutions p B) :
    HasFullSetAlgebraicSolutions A := by
  sorry

end GrothendieckKatzPCurvatureConjecture
modeling_decisions: Used the article's essential case: square systems dY/dz = A Y with A over RatFunc ℚ, rather than the broader number-field/smooth-variety formulation, because the source says the latter reduces to this same question.
Interpreted “almost all p” as the cofinite filter on the subtype Nat.Primes, not as infinitely many primes.

Made good reduction explicit via a common quotient presentation by integer polynomials whose denominator stays nonzero modulo p. Required existence of such a reduced matrix and the mod-p solution condition at every prime in the cofinite set.
Used the equivalent mod-p criterion stated in the decomposition notes: an invertible fundamental matrix over 𝔽_p(z), rather than defining p-curvature recursively.

Represented a full set of algebraic solutions by an invertible fundamental matrix in an algebraic closure of ℚ(z). A derivation linear over ℚ and sending the embedded variable z to 1 encodes the unique extension of d/dz.
Allowed n = 0; the empty system has the expected empty invertible fundamental matrix and does not alter the conjecture.
